page.title: Board
page.subtitle: Three parallel plans, separate targets and satisfaction

plans.title: Three plans run in parallel
plans.body: Switch between the 1-, 3- and 5-year plans with the tabs. One plan at a time, full width. Each shows its standing, satisfaction, sponsor× modifier and targets with status icons. Click a target to see the board's reaction.

satisfaction.title: Satisfaction drives sponsor and consequences
satisfaction.body: High satisfaction (over 70%) boosts sponsor income. Low satisfaction (under 40%) can trigger salary caps, signing restrictions and ultimately forced rider sales. The progression is gradual and predictable.

kpis.title: What they evaluate on
kpis.body: Results, finances, identity (U25, national core) and ranking, plus newer types: monuments, jerseys, star rider and U25 stat gains. Your club DNA and 5 named board members colour the reactions.

baseline.title: The board is observing your first season
baseline.body: You are in your baseline season. The board is learning your team with no demands or targets. Sponsor modifier stays at 1.0×. When the season ends, negotiations open sequentially: first the 5-year plan, then the 3-year plan, then the 1-year plan.

emptyState.headline: Meet your board
emptyState.intro: You do not have any board plans yet. The board sets targets, evaluates your season and decides how much sponsor income your team gets paid out.

oneYear.label: 1-year plan
oneYear.description: Strict targets, fast results. Full penalty on failure.

threeYear.label: 3-year plan
threeYear.description: Moderate targets, room to grow. 20% reduced penalty.

emptyState.plansFooter: All three plans run in parallel. You negotiate one at a time, and each has its own targets and time horizon.
emptyState.satisfactionFooter: Every met target boosts satisfaction. Dissatisfied boards tighten requirements at the next plan negotiation.

goalHelp.heading: How is this measured?
goalHelp.signature_rider: Counts riders the board recognizes as star riders, using the same bar as the board's star-rider count: renown weighted with UCI points, combined into one score. Renown counts more than points, so a well-known rider can qualify without a big point haul.
goalHelp.top_n_finish: Evaluated on your final standing in the last season of the plan, not an average across the plan's seasons.
goalHelp.u25_development_delta: The average stat-point gain per U25 rider per season. Develop young riders so their stats rise over the season.

drivers.heading: What drives this board?
drivers.weightHint: Meeting these goals moves board satisfaction more than the others.

dna.selectIntro: The board has observed season 1 and suggests three directions. DNA shapes target weighting, club tradition targets and which board members you get from the first plan.

rechoose.hint: You can still change your club DNA until your first season ends. After that it's locked in.
rechoose.heading: Change your club DNA
rechoose.intro: Pick a different direction while you're still in your first season. Switching re-assigns your board members and target weighting.

locked.heading: Locked for the season
locked.body: Your club DNA is set for the season and can't be changed. It shapes target weighting, club tradition targets and which board members you get.

skandinavisk_udvikling.label: Scandinavian development team
skandinavisk_udvikling.longDescription: We build riders from the ground up: patience, structure and Nordic work ethic. Sponsors expect development, not fireworks.
skandinavisk_udvikling.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: develop the talents, average +3 stat points per season for U25 riders

italiensk_klassiker.label: Italian classics traditionalist
italiensk_klassiker.shortDescription: Spring is sacred. Monuments are the goal
italiensk_klassiker.longDescription: The club is built on the roads of Lombardia and Strade Bianche. Our fans dream of Sanremo and Lombardia, not Tour de France podiums.
italiensk_klassiker.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: at least one podium in a classic (incl. Monuments) per plan cycle

sprint_kommerciel.label: Sprint-focused commercial team
sprint_kommerciel.shortDescription: Wins at the line, sponsors on the wheel
sprint_kommerciel.longDescription: Our rider should be first across the line and first in front of the cameras. Sponsor growth comes from visibility, and visibility comes from stage wins.
sprint_kommerciel.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: win at least 2 stage-race jerseys over the plan period (sprint focus)

fransk_klatrer.label: French climbing heritage
fransk_klatrer.shortDescription: The Tour mountains are the club's home
fransk_klatrer.longDescription: We have climbed with Anquetil, Hinault and Pinot. The mountains define us, and the Tour de France is still the most important Sunday on the calendar.
fransk_klatrer.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: at least 4 French riders in the squad

britisk_allrounder.label: British all-rounder
britisk_allrounder.shortDescription: Discipline across the board, data-led and broad
britisk_allrounder.longDescription: The Sky school lives on. We win through structure, marginal gains and depth, from Roubaix to Andorra. No discipline owns the club, but every discipline belongs here.
britisk_allrounder.traditionGoalLabel: Club DNA: top 3 in the division (broad performance)

suggestionRationale.wildcard: A new path. The board will follow wherever it leads

expired.summary: The board will negotiate a new plan based on the latest evaluation and the team's current direction.

awaitingFirstMarkers.summary: {personalitySummary} For now expectations are intact, but the sporting answers only come once the season takes shape.{profileHint}

veryHappy.summary: {strong} is driving the plan forward, and {weakLower} is still under control.

steadyProgress.headline: The board sees steady progress
steadyProgress.summary: {strong} is on track, but {weakLower} needs more focus to keep the plan healthy.

awaitingNext.summary: {weak} is lagging behind the plan, and the pressure rises if the trend does not turn soon.

concerned.headline: The board is concerned

signalHint.nationalCoreStrong: The {country} core gives the team a clear identity in the board's eyes.
signalHint.nationalCoreWeak: The {country} core still gives the team a clear identity the board will not let go of easily.
signalHint.starHigh: Big-name riders strengthen the sponsor project, but they also keep expectations high.
signalHint.starHighWeak: Big-name riders keep the sponsors interested, but they also push the board to demand more output.
signalHint.starMedium: The team's profiles give the sponsor project a little extra weight.

sponsoraten.label: The Sponsor Director
sponsoraten.shortDescription: Guards sponsor relationships and financial discipline
sponsoraten.longDescription: A former commercial director. Keeps an eye on sponsor deals, the balance sheet and financial risk. Grows nervous around debt and crosses his fingers for sponsor growth every season.

feedback_positive: The sponsors are happy. This holds up.
Now we can finally show the numbers off.
This looks like a well-run project.
Earnings are keeping up with the ambition, perfect.
The board can rest easy now.
feedback_warning: We need to watch the balance from here.
The sponsors are eyeing the numbers nervously.
We should not chase results on borrowed time.
Luck is not a plan, we need stability.
If this turns, it gets expensive.
feedback_negative: This will not hold in the long run.
The sponsors are calling, and not to praise us.
The numbers are saying what we do not want to hear.
We lose trust every time this repeats.
If this continues, there is no budget next year.
goal_proposal: This secures the cash flow.
The sponsor deal will reward this.
Realistic and budget-friendly, yes please.
This gives us room to plan.
Conservative, but that is the strength.
goal_achievement: Exactly what we hoped for, good work.
The sponsors called us themselves to say thanks.
This keeps the budget down to the last detail.
Solid numbers, this is how we build on.
Trust grows with every quarter.
goal_failure: We miss it again, and the sponsors feel it.
This is no longer just an accounting problem.
We are bleeding more than expected.
The investors are asking questions now.
This puts next season's sponsor negotiation at risk.
receipt_positive: The budget holds, and the sponsors are calling to renew.
We hit the target without touching the reserve.
Three quarters in the black in a row. That is not luck, that is discipline.
The books look better than my forecast. That is rare.
receipt_negative: We are dipping into the reserve again. That number needs to turn.
Sponsor income is under budget for the third month running.
I cannot defend this number at the next meeting.
The debt is growing faster than the revenue. That is not sustainable.
meeting_easier: A lower target means a lower ceiling for the sponsors. I will take it, but I am noting it.
This is the cautious road. Fine by me.
Eased, but still a number I can stand behind to the sponsors.
I prefer a target we hit over one we chase.
meeting_keep: Same number, same expectation. I respect that.
No change to the budget, no change in how I am watching.
We hold the course. That is often the right call.
Kept, as it should be while the numbers still add up.
meeting_stretch: A higher target needs better books behind it. Show me that.
I am tightening my watch exactly as much as the target is tightened.
Ambitious. The sponsors will ask how we are funding it.
A stretch target I accept, but I am keeping the books on every month.
midseason_status: We are halfway. The numbers on the table today are ones I can stand behind.
Halfway through the season, and the board wants an honest picture, not a dressed up one.
This status is not a verdict. It is a snapshot we act on.
I have seen worse halfway books than this.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and the books confirm it. That is rare, both at once.
We celebrate this, and then the board finds the next target for the empty slot.
Reached ahead of schedule. The sponsors notice that kind of thing.
A closed chapter with a clean set of books. Good work.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and it costs trust, not just the number.
We have to look these numbers in the eye without dressing them up.
Not catastrophic, but the board expected more by now.
I am writing it down. We will take it up again at the next annual meeting.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. The numbers cannot wait for the next annual meeting.
This is not routine. We meet now, not at the usual time.
I asked for an extra meeting. The books require it.
We are gathering off cycle, because something here cannot wait.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair with the books in order. That is the legacy I wanted.
My time as chairman ends here. Look after the numbers after me.
I am stepping down. The club's finances stand better than when I took over.
The chair moves on. I will keep my worries to myself from here.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read the books.
New chairman, same demands on the numbers.
I am going into this with my eyes open and the calculator ready.
It is my turn now. I promise no miracles, only an honest set of books.

traditionalisten.label: The Traditionalist
traditionalisten.shortDescription: Weighs the club's heritage and national identity
traditionalisten.longDescription: Sits on the board because he was there in the previous century, or nearly. Wants the club to remind people where it came from. Least enthusiastic about modern flair.

feedback_positive: The club carries its heritage with pride.
This is what the board dreamed of back in the 90s.
The team looks like itself again.
People recognise the club in the peloton.
The soul is intact, that is what matters most.
feedback_warning: We are losing ourselves a little in the chase.
Where has the club's identity gone?
This looks more like other teams than ours.
Tradition is not a bonus box.
Something recognisable is missing.
feedback_negative: We have become a stranger on our own road.
The club is no longer recognisable.
It is like watching another club ride in our jersey.
This is a break with everything the club stands for.
Our fans are weeping, and I nearly am too.
goal_proposal: This looks like the club's DNA.
That is how it has always been with us.
Our fans will feel it.
It is continuity, yes.
The board recognises the club in this.
goal_achievement: True club spirit, this is how it should be.
The forefathers would smile.
This is why we exist.
This is how you build a club that lasts.
The identity stands clearer now.
goal_failure: It is a hard blow to the heritage.
We owe the club an apology.
This would never have happened in the old days.
We are losing ground on the home turf we own.
Where has the pride gone?
receipt_positive: The club still looks like itself. That is worth more than any single result.
We are writing another page the old guard would recognize.
This is the club I signed up to protect, alive and well.
History does not repeat itself here, it continues.
receipt_negative: We are drifting from what this club has always stood for.
The badge deserves better than this.
I do not recognize us in this.
The old members would not stand for this, and neither should we.
meeting_easier: A lighter target does not erase our history. I can live with that.
The club has survived quieter seasons than this before.
Eased, but the crest on the jersey stays the same.
Fine, as long as we do not ease off what we stand for.
meeting_keep: Kept as is. Continuity is half of what this club is.
No change, and the old members would approve of that steadiness.
We hold the line the way the club always has.
Same target. This club does not chase every new trend.
meeting_stretch: A bigger ambition, as long as it still looks like us when we get there.
Stretch it, but do not stretch away from who we are.
I accept a harder target for a club with this much history behind it.
Ambitious, and the archives will remember which era did this.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and the club still looks like the one on the old photographs.
This status report belongs in the club's own history, good or bad.
We are judged at midseason the same way every board before us was judged.
Halfway, and I still recognize the team we sent out in spring.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and it belongs in the club's own record books.
Another chapter written the way the founders would have wanted.
This is the kind of moment the old members talk about for years.
Reached, and the history of this club just grew a little longer.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and it hurts more here than a number should.
This club has faced worse and stayed itself. It will again.
We owe the old members better than a missed milestone.
Not the ending this chapter deserved. We write the next one properly.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. Some things cannot wait for the calendar.
This is not routine, and the club's history says we act when it matters.
I asked for us to gather now. The badge is worth an early meeting.
Extraordinary meeting, because the club deserves more than a shrug.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. The club stood here long before me and will stand long after.
My time ends here, but the history I was trusted with continues.
I am stepping down having kept the club looking like itself. That was the job.
The chair moves on. Someone else carries the old flag now.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read the club's own history.
New chairman, same respect for what came before me.
I am going into this knowing exactly whose shoulders I stand on.
It is my turn now. I promise to leave the badge exactly as proud as I found it.

talentspejderen.label: The Talent Scout
talentspejderen.longDescription: A former sporting director for a development team. Would rather see a 22-year-old win five years from now than a 32-year-old win today. Knows every U25 stat by heart.

feedback_positive: The talents get room, and they deliver.
This is exactly how you build the future.
In five years everyone will understand this choice.
The youth is blossoming, rarely seen this clearly.
The next generation is stepping up now.
feedback_warning: We must not forget the youth in the chase.
The talents are getting too little racing.
Where is the U25 rotation?
We have better riders in the second team than we are showing.
We are selling the future for a single win.
feedback_negative: We are leaving a whole generation on the bench.
The young riders burn out without racing in their legs.
This is no future for the club.
The talents will flee to other teams next year.
We have misunderstood what a team is.
goal_proposal: This opens doors for the young riders.
Mapped-out development, we will take it.
The young riders need exactly this.
This is how you grow a team organically.
This will lift more than one board metric.
goal_achievement: The talents delivered, just as predicted.
This development creates decades of value.
The U25s have taken the step, wonderful to see.
This is how you send a signal to the scouts.
This confirms the whole development philosophy.
goal_failure: The young riders did not get the chance, our mistake.
We carry the blame for stalled development.
Talent takes longer to recover from this.
We lost something we built over years.
Better rotation would have solved this.
receipt_positive: I flagged that rider two seasons ago. The numbers are finally catching up to the eye test.
Another name from my list is starting to deliver.
This is exactly the kind of potential I scout for, showing up on schedule.
Found early, developed patiently, and now it shows.
receipt_negative: A talent I flagged is stalling, and that is on the development plan, not the rider.
The potential is real. The pathway to use it is not.
I do not scout riders to watch them sit still.
Somewhere a scout at another club is writing down the name we are wasting.
meeting_easier: A lower bar buys the pipeline more time to mature, I will take that trade.
Eased, and that means fewer forced calls on riders who are not ready yet.
Fine by me. Potential needs patience more than pressure.
I would rather protect the long game than chase this season's number.
meeting_keep: Same target. My scouting list does not change on a whim either.
Kept as is, and the projections I have made still hold.
No change needed, the pipeline is on the timeline I mapped out.
Fine, the numbers I am tracking do not need a new target to move.
meeting_stretch: A higher bar is fine if it does not force a half-ready name onto the start list.
Stretch it, but do not stretch a nineteen-year-old past what the data says he can take.
I accept it, as long as the pipeline gets the time it needs behind it.
Ambitious, and I will hold the club to protecting development while chasing it.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I want to know which names on my list actually got minutes.
The status report should show me curves, not just this week's placings.
I measure this season by how many prospects moved up my list, not just the table.
Halfway, and three names I flagged in preseason are trending exactly as projected.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and a name from my old shortlist made it happen.
This proves the scouting model works, not just the roster.
Reached, and it started as a hunch on a spreadsheet three years ago.
This is the payoff for betting on potential before the results existed.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and I am checking whether the pipeline was ever given a real chance.
Not catastrophic, but a few names on my list needed more minutes than they got.
We owe the development pathway a harder look before the next attempt.
I am noting which prospects were held back. That data does not disappear.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting, and I want the pipeline's needs on the table.
This cannot wait, and neither can the window some of these prospects have.
I asked for us to gather now. A scouting window does not reopen on request.
Extraordinary meeting, because a decision here shapes names on my list for years.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. The shortlist I built stays behind for whoever follows.
My time ends here, but the names I flagged keep developing without me.
I am stepping down having found more talent than I got credit for.
The chair moves on. Keep an eye on the ones I marked, they are not done yet.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is read every scouting report on file.
New chairman, same eye for what a rider could become in three years.
I am going into this looking past this season's roster, toward the next one.
It is my turn now. I promise to find the names nobody else was watching yet.

resultatjaegeren.label: The Results Hunter
resultatjaegeren.shortDescription: Wants to win now, everything else is excuses
resultatjaegeren.longDescription: An ex-sporting director with three Tour podiums on his CV. Patience is not a personal strength. Judges a team on wins, podiums and points totals, full stop.

feedback_positive: Wins. Finally, wins.
This is what I was hired to see.
The results speak for themselves.
The rivals are looking nervous now.
This is a winning team, finally.
feedback_warning: The wins are too few and too small.
We are racing top-10 but not top-3.
Taking part is not enough.
The rivals do not feel us yet.
Where is the killer edge that wins races?
feedback_negative: This is unacceptable.
The results are a disaster.
We are invisible in the peloton.
This team should win more, much more.
How many races must we lose before we act?
goal_proposal: Finally, something with teeth.
We win this, or we swap the bikes out.
That is how you set demands.
We will take it. Next target?
The chase is what makes it fun, bring it on.
goal_achievement: The win is in the bag, keep going.
This is the club we know from the good years.
The rivals saw it coming, and could not stop us.
Finally we are delivering, keep going.
This is what the board was elected to see.
goal_failure: This is embarrassing.
We lost to teams we should crush.
Step forward and explain.
That is not a team, it is an excuse.
The next plan sharpens the demands considerably.
receipt_positive: A win is a win. Keep them coming.
We are climbing the standings, and that is the only chart I read.
Podiums. Finally something worth talking about.
This is what winning looks like. More of it.
receipt_negative: No wins is no wins. Excuses do not count on a scoreboard.
We are slipping down the table, and I do not accept slow.
Second place is the first loser, and we have collected too many of those.
This losing streak needs to end this week, not next.
meeting_easier: A lower target still needs to end in wins, or it is not a target.
Fine, but easy still means a win at the finish line, not a good try.
Eased, and I expect it back up the moment we start winning.
I accept it grudgingly. This club does not aim low for long.
meeting_keep: Same target. Winning does not need a discount.
Kept, because the standard should not move for anyone.
No change. We were hired to win, not to renegotiate.
Fine, the number stays. Now go win it.
meeting_stretch: A harder target. Finally somebody in this room wants to win.
Stretch it. I would have asked for more anyway.
Good. Ambition is the only thing I ever agree to without a fight.
Set it higher. This club should be uncomfortable chasing anything less.
midseason_status: Halfway, and I am counting wins, not effort.
This status report is one number to me: how many times have we won.
Midseason is not for excuses. It is for a scoreboard.
Halfway through, and I want more wins than we have in the second half.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, because we won when it mattered.
Finally a milestone that matches what this club should be doing.
Reached. Now find the next one, higher.
This is what the board should always look like: wins on the board.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and that is unacceptable at this level.
We had the roster to hit this. We did not hit it. Explain that.
Missing this costs more than the milestone itself. It costs credibility.
Next attempt gets a sharper target and zero patience for excuses.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. Losing streaks like this do not wait for the calendar.
This is not routine. We meet now, because the standings do not fix themselves.
I demanded an extra meeting. Nobody loses this many races without a hard conversation.
Extraordinary meeting, because acceptable is not a word I use about this record.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. Judge me on the wins, that was always the deal.
My time ends here. I never asked to be liked, only to win.
I am stepping down. The trophy cabinet says whether I did my job.
The chair moves on. Whoever takes it should want to win as badly as I did.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is look at last season's results.
New chairman, same demand: win now, explain never.
I am going into this to win, not to manage expectations.
It is my turn now. I promise nothing except that losing will not be comfortable here.

pragmatikeren.label: The Pragmatist
pragmatikeren.shortDescription: Seeks the balance between ambition and caution
pragmatikeren.longDescription: A former industry board chair. Looks at everything as a risk and reward ratio. Rarely euphoric, rarely panicked, rarely in agreement with himself two days running.

feedback_positive: This looks like a healthy balance.
Risk and reward are matched well.
The team is delivering on several fronts, good.
It is sustainable, which is what we are after.
No red flags, plenty of green.
feedback_warning: This is on a knife's edge, keep watch.
We are losing a little on every front.
It is balancing too close to the edge.
A little more discipline and it turns.
We are missing one metric that pulls its weight.
feedback_negative: The risk outweighs the reward considerably.
This will not survive another stress test.
We are losing on both sides of the table.
This is not a plan anymore, it is drift.
The board cannot defend this.
goal_proposal: Realistic, we back it.
It matches where we are now.
That is how you avoid overstretching.
It is pragmatic and clear, yes.
This is a good middle path.
goal_achievement: As expected, solid work.
This is what pragmatism is for.
The team delivered without drama.
This is what sustainability looks like.
The next target can be built on top of this.
goal_failure: This should have been within reach.
Disappointing, with no clear excuses.
We will choose the next plan with tighter demands.
This worries me more than it should.
The board expects an open evaluation.
receipt_positive: The risk and the reward finally line up. That is all I ever ask for.
Nothing spectacular, but nothing exposed either. I will take that.
This is the kind of balanced week that actually builds something.
We are winning on more fronts than we are losing on. Good enough is good.
receipt_negative: The scale has tipped, and I do not like which way.
We are losing a little on every front. That adds up faster than one big loss.
This is not a crisis yet, but it stops being fine if it repeats.
The trade-off we accepted is not paying off the way it should.
meeting_easier: A lower target is a fair trade for a season that needs room to breathe.
Eased, and that is a reasonable adjustment, not a retreat.
I can live with lower, as long as it is a decision and not a drift.
Fine. Sometimes the balanced choice is the smaller number.
meeting_keep: Same target. It was balanced when we set it, and nothing has changed that.
Kept as is. I do not move a number just because someone is impatient.
No change needed, the trade-off still holds up under scrutiny.
Fine as it stands. A steady target is worth more than a reactive one.
meeting_stretch: A higher target, as long as we are honest about what we are risking for it.
Stretch it, but I want the downside written down before we sign.
I accept it if the upside genuinely outweighs what could go wrong.
Ambitious is fine. Reckless is not, and I will keep an eye on the line.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and the picture is neither as good nor as bad as it feels.
This status is a snapshot, not a verdict. Let us treat it that way.
Some things are up, some are down. That is a normal season, not a crisis.
Halfway, and the balance still holds, barely, which is exactly why we watch it.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and the trade-offs along the way were worth it.
Reached without breaking anything else to get there. That is the real win.
This is what a balanced plan looks like when it pays off.
Good outcome, and I would make the same trade-offs again.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips. Not the end of the plan, but worth a hard look at why.
We miscalculated the trade-off somewhere. Let us find where.
Disappointing, but not a reason to abandon the balanced approach.
I am noting it. The next plan adjusts the weighting, not the philosophy.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. The balance has tipped enough to warrant it.
This is not routine, but it is not panic either. We are simply adjusting early.
I asked for an earlier meeting because waiting would cost more than meeting does.
Extraordinary meeting, weighed calmly against waiting for the usual date.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair with the books and the roster both in reasonable shape.
My time ends here. I never chased the spectacular, only the sustainable.
I am stepping down having kept more balances steady than tipped over.
The chair moves on. Whoever follows should weigh both sides, always.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is weigh what is working against what is not.
New chairman, same instinct to look for the trade-off before the headline.
I am going into this looking for balance, not applause.
It is my turn now. I promise measured decisions, not dramatic ones.

ungdomsidealisten.label: The Youth Idealist
ungdomsidealisten.shortDescription: The club's future is built on young legs
ungdomsidealisten.longDescription: A teacher and former coach in the lower-division system. Wants the club to be known for nurturing talent, without selling it off afterwards. Understands that every winner was young once.

feedback_positive: The young riders get room, that is what it is all about.
The club is a hatchery for the future.
The U25 imprint is clear and beautiful.
Talent grows here, as it should.
This will be remembered fondly.
feedback_warning: We are pushing the young riders into too much racing.
Or, is there even room for U25 at all?
Talent without patience burns out.
We are losing focus on what matters most, the youth.
Where is the long-term line?
feedback_negative: The young riders are suffering, it is heartbreaking to watch.
The club is selling its own future.
This team has forgotten where it came from.
The talents are fleeing to places where they are seen.
We are betraying a whole generation right now.
goal_proposal: This gives the young riders room, perfect.
The board is 100% behind it.
That is how you build the future.
This will bear fruit in years to come.
The U25s will feel seen by this.
goal_achievement: The young riders took responsibility, and delivered.
This is the reward for patience.
We have created an environment they blossom in.
The club can be proud of its development work.
This is what a healthy generation looks like.
goal_failure: We did not give them enough room, regrettably.
This is a hard lesson for the whole system.
We owe the young riders a better structure.
A damaging signal to future talents.
If this continues, the academy will not call.
receipt_positive: A debutant took his first win today. That is the whole point of this.
The young riders get room, and they are using it.
Another U25 rider took a step today. That is how a generation is built.
This team is developing talent, not just spending it.
receipt_negative: The young riders are on the bench again. That is hard to watch.
We promise development and deliver standing still.
Another debutant without race days in his legs this month.
The talent is there. The chance is not.
meeting_easier: An eased target means more patience with the young riders. I will gladly take that.
Fewer points to chase, more room to let a debutant learn.
Eased is fine, as long as the development is not eased along with it.
I accept this, if it means more races for the U25 squad.
meeting_keep: Same target, same promise to the young riders that they are seen.
Kept as is. The young riders deserve consistency, not shifting ground.
No change, and that is fine. Development takes the time it takes.
We hold the course for the sake of the youth.
meeting_stretch: A tighter target must not come at the expense of the debutants.
I accept the stretch target, but I am watching who gets to race.
Ambitious is fine, as long as the young riders still get their chance.
Set the target higher. Just do not forget who has to reach it.
midseason_status: We are halfway, and I want to know how many debutants have raced since last time.
The halfway picture should show development, not just placings.
I measure the season by how many young riders moved forward, not only by podiums.
Halfway through, and the young riders still have my full attention.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and a debutant helped make it happen. That is how it should look.
Reached, and the board is already finding the next target for the young riders to grow toward.
This proves the development path works.
A future that was promised is now a future that was delivered.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and I ask myself if the young riders got enough time.
Not the end of the world, but the development needs to speed up.
We owe the young riders a better plan from here.
I am noting it. The next annual meeting needs to give them a real chance again.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. I want the young riders' conditions on the agenda.
This meeting cannot wait, and neither can the development work.
I asked for us to gather now. The talent must not suffer while we wait.
Extraordinary meeting, because something here hits the young riders directly.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. Take good care of the academy after me.
My time ends here, but the young riders I made room for keep growing.
I am stepping down with a clear conscience. The youth got their chance under me.
The chair moves on. Do not forget who is building the future.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the young riders get my full attention from day one.
New chairman, same belief that the future starts in the U25 squad.
I am going into this for the sake of the young riders, not my own.
It is my turn now. I promise room for those who have not had their chance yet.

nationalist_purist.label: The Nationalist Purist
nationalist_purist.shortDescription: The club should represent its home country
nationalist_purist.longDescription: A former national-team coach. Believes a club without a national core is just a sponsor in jerseys. Would rather have one home-grown talent than two foreign stars.

feedback_positive: The home-grown core still shines.
We are the club from our country, no doubt about it.
The home-soil pride is intact.
Our fans hear their own language in the peloton.
This is how a club should sound.
feedback_warning: Our national identity is slipping away.
Fewer home-grown riders, that matters.
We are losing the connection to the fan base.
Home and club should be closely tied.
Where is the next local star?
feedback_negative: The club has become an airport of sponsors.
The national connection is broken.
The fans can no longer see themselves in the team.
This is a commercial transaction, not a club.
We are ashamed of how the roster is put together.
goal_proposal: Home colours, of course.
This affirms the club's roots.
The board stands firmly behind this.
This is how the club stays itself.
It is what the original sponsor would have chosen.
goal_achievement: The home-grown core delivered, fantastic.
This will resonate across the whole country.
This is how you become a national treasure.
Every home win is worth twice as much.
This makes the club irreplaceable.
goal_failure: The home country's gaze weighs heavy now.
This wounds the club at its core.
We have let down more than just the board.
This makes recruitment harder.
We are losing ground we cannot win back easily.
receipt_positive: Our own riders carried the flag today, and the fans heard their own language in the bunch.
This is a home-grown result, and that matters more than the points.
The national core delivered, exactly as a club like ours should.
Our flag was at the front today. That is worth more than the margin.
receipt_negative: Fewer home riders on the results sheet, and fewer fans see themselves in this team.
We are becoming a club of imported names, and the home crowd notices.
The national core is thinning, and that is a slower disaster than any loss.
Our own flag is drifting toward the back of the peloton.
meeting_easier: A lower target for the national core, as long as the core itself does not shrink.
Eased, but I want the home riders still on the start list, not just the number.
Fine, so long as it is patience with our own, not a quiet retreat from them.
I accept it, if it buys the home talent more time to grow into the role.
meeting_keep: Same target. Our national identity does not get renegotiated on a whim.
Kept as is, and the home fans deserve that consistency.
No change. The flag on the jersey stays exactly as important as before.
Fine as it stands. This club's core was never up for discount.
meeting_stretch: A higher target for the national core, and I will hold everyone to it.
Stretch it. It is about time this club leaned harder into who we are.
I accept it, as long as it means more home names, not just a bigger number.
Ambitious, and the home fans will finally see themselves more often.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I want to know how many home riders actually raced.
This status means little to me without a count of our own flag on the start lists.
I measure the season by how much of this team still feels like home.
Halfway, and the national core is holding, which is the number that matters to me.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and a home rider was at the front when it happened.
Reached, and the whole country gets to claim this one.
This is the kind of milestone that makes the home fans proud to wear the colors.
Our own flag delivered when it counted. That will be remembered.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and I ask whether the home riders were given the chance to carry it.
Not catastrophic, but the national core deserved better positioning here.
We owe the home fans a clearer path to this milestone next time.
I am noting it. The flag comes back to the front at the next annual meeting.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting, and I want the national core's standing on the agenda.
This cannot wait, and neither can a fading connection to the home fans.
I asked for us to gather now. Our identity is not something we let drift while we wait.
Extraordinary meeting, because something here touches what this club is supposed to represent.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. The flag still flies at the front, and that was always the mission.
My time ends here, but the home core I protected keeps carrying this club.
I am stepping down with the national identity intact. That is my legacy here.
The chair moves on. Do not let the home core become an afterthought after me.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is count how many home riders are on this roster.
New chairman, same belief that a club without a national core is just a sponsor in jerseys.
I am going into this for the home fans, the ones who see themselves in this team.
It is my turn now. I promise the flag stays at the front of every conversation.

klassiker_purist.label: The Classics Purist
klassiker_purist.shortDescription: Monuments are what make a club immortal
klassiker_purist.longDescription: A former classics rider himself. Believes GC racing is statistics, Roubaix is history. Would rather have one Monument than five stage wins.

feedback_positive: We are heading for a Monument, I can feel it.
The classics spirit hangs in the air.
This is where the club belongs.
Rock-solid roles for the spring campaign.
Rare quality on the roads that count.
feedback_warning: The classics ambition is too soft.
We are missing a hard man for the Roubaix type.
Where is the spring focus?
This team would never win Liège.
That is stage racing, not the heritage.
feedback_negative: We are classics-less, this is embarrassing.
The spring months vanish without a trace.
The team rides past the Monuments without looking up.
This is the wrong club identity for this sport.
We will not be remembered for any of this.
goal_proposal: Monuments, finally on the agenda.
This is what the club was born for.
Spring focus, the board is cheering.
This is how you write history.
We will take it and ride home with a cobblestone.
goal_achievement: A Monument! This is where sport becomes eternal.
This goes in the books forever.
The spring is ours, as it should be.
Cobble by cobble, that is how you build a club.
This is the kind of thing members remember.
goal_failure: The spring campaign flopped, unacceptable.
The Monuments are laughing at us this year.
This rips the heart out of the classics soul.
We need to reinvent the spring plan.
No one takes the club seriously on the Roubaix ramp after this.
receipt_positive: That was a proper cobbled performance. The spring campaign is alive.
We rode like a classics team today, and it showed on the stones.
A result like that belongs on the Roubaix velodrome, not just the results sheet.
This is what a monument-shaped season looks like in April.
receipt_negative: No cobbles, no spring form, no story worth telling this April.
We looked lost the moment the road turned to stones.
A classics team that avoids the cobbles is not a classics team.
The Monuments will not remember a season like this one.
meeting_easier: A lighter spring target, as long as we still show up for the stones that matter.
Eased, but the Monuments do not care about our excuses either way.
Fine, if it means we build properly toward Roubaix instead of forcing it.
I accept it, as long as classics identity is not what got lowered.
meeting_keep: Same target. The cobbles do not get easier because we ask nicely.
Kept as is. Spring does not renegotiate its calendar for anyone.
No change. A classics club holds its ambition through the mud.
Fine as it stands. The Monuments deserve a fixed target, not a moving one.
meeting_stretch: A harder spring target. Finally something worthy of the cobbles.
Stretch it. This club should be uncomfortable aiming at anything less than a Monument.
I accept it, gladly. The classics deserve real ambition, not a modest one.
Ambitious, and the spring campaign just got the pressure it needed.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I am still judging this season on what happened in April.
The status report matters less to me than whether we had a real spring.
This club lives or dies on the cobbles, and the rest of the season is just aftermath.
Halfway, and the Monuments already told us most of what we need to know.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and it happened on the roads that matter to this club.
Reached, with cobbles under the wheels. That is how it should be done.
This is the kind of milestone the classics history books will actually mention.
A monument-worthy result. That is what this club exists for.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and a spring without a real result stings more than any other season.
Not catastrophic, but the cobbled campaign owed us more than this.
We owe the classics identity a sharper spring next year.
I am noting it. The next attempt starts building for April immediately.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. Spring does not wait for the usual calendar.
This is not routine, but neither is losing our shot at the Monuments.
I asked for us to gather now. A cobbled campaign built in a rush never wins anything.
Extraordinary meeting, because April is closer than the board seems to think.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. We chased the Monuments honestly, and that was the whole point.
My time ends here, but the classics spirit I fought for should not leave with me.
I am stepping down having never once let this club forget the cobbles.
The chair moves on. Whoever follows had better still believe in April.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is check the spring calendar.
New chairman, same belief that Roubaix means more than any stage race podium.
I am going into this for the cobbles, the ones that made me love this sport.
It is my turn now. I promise this club will not forget what April is for.

gc_elsker.label: The GC Romantic
gc_elsker.shortDescription: Three weeks or nothing, the Tour is everything
gc_elsker.longDescription: A former GC director. The board's biggest dreamer. Wants to build the team up to win a Grand Tour. Does not understand why anyone bothers racing otherwise.

feedback_positive: The GC path is set, we are building towards the Tour.
This is a true grand-tour-rider build.
The mountains are waiting for us.
The three-week form is starting to shine.
We have a team that can win big.
feedback_warning: The GC structure is too soft.
Where are the domestiques for the high mountains?
We lack the third-week resilience.
This team cracks in the Pyrenees.
The Tour dream is on pause.
feedback_negative: We do not have a GC man on the team, unacceptable.
This team would lose 20 minutes on day one.
The Tour is further away than ever.
The board did not get what we were promised.
This is not a serious World Tour project.
goal_proposal: GC focus, finally heading for the big game.
This is where the career is built.
The Tour is the goal, and this is the step.
The board accepts without hesitation.
This is how you raise a captain project.
goal_achievement: The GC result is solid, keep climbing.
This is what roads to the Tour are built on.
The mountains gave respect, good work.
We are heading for the chapter everyone will read.
This is the step before the three weeks.
goal_failure: The GC project is bleeding, this does not help.
We are further from the Tour now than before the season.
This is a regression, not an adjustment.
The mountains crushed us, this must never happen again.
We lack a plan for where the star is going to come from.
receipt_positive: That climb was Tour form. We are building something real for July.
The GC picture looks better every week. This is how a stage-race project is built.
A performance like that belongs in the mountains of a Grand Tour, not a one-day race.
We are riding like a team with a three-week ambition, finally.
receipt_negative: No GC presence, no mountain legs, no Tour project worth the name.
We fell apart the moment the road went uphill for more than a stage.
A team without a real GC threat is not building toward anything I care about.
The Tour is further away this week than it was last month.
meeting_easier: A lighter GC target, as long as we still ride the three weeks like they matter.
Eased, but I want the mountain legs built regardless of the number.
Fine, if it buys the climbers time before we ask them for a Grand Tour.
I accept it, as long as the Tour is still the horizon we are riding toward.
meeting_keep: Same target. The mountains do not care whether we feel like it this week.
Kept as is. A three-week project does not renegotiate its own timeline.
No change. The Tour is not moved back because we asked for a discount.
Fine as it stands. GC ambition should not be the first thing we cut.
meeting_stretch: A higher GC target. Finally something with a Tour-sized ambition.
Stretch it. This club should always be aiming at three weeks, not one day.
I accept it gladly. The mountains deserve real ambition behind them.
Ambitious, and that is the only setting this project should run in.
midseason_status: Halfway through, and I am judging this season on where the GC project stands, not the sprints.
The status report matters less than whether we have a real leader for July.
This club exists for three weeks in summer. Everything else is preparation.
Halfway, and the mountain legs are coming, which is the only number I track.
milestone_achieved: The milestone is reached, and it happened with real GC weight behind it.
Reached, on the kind of climb that decides a Grand Tour.
This is the kind of result that says the Tour project is real, not a dream.
A three-week-worthy result. That is what this club is built to chase.
milestone_missed: The milestone slips, and a Grand Tour project without it loses a whole season of momentum.
Not catastrophic, but the mountains owed us more than this.
We owe the GC project a sharper build toward next year's three weeks.
I am noting it. The road to the Tour starts being rebuilt today.
extraordinary_meeting: The board is calling an extraordinary meeting. A Tour project does not wait for the usual calendar.
This is not routine, but neither is losing our shot at three weeks in July.
I asked for us to gather now. Mountain legs are not built in a rush at the last minute.
Extraordinary meeting, because the Tour is closer than the board seems to think.
chairman_departure: I am leaving the chair. We built toward the mountains honestly, and that was the whole point.
My time ends here, but the Tour ambition I fought for should not leave with me.
I am stepping down having never once let this club forget what three weeks means.
The chair moves on. Whoever follows had better still dream about July.
chairman_arrival: I am taking the chair, and the first thing I do is check who can survive three weeks in the mountains.
New chairman, same belief that nothing in this sport matters more than the Tour.
I am going into this for July, the only month that really counts.
It is my turn now. I promise this club will not forget what three weeks means.

lower_results_pressure.label: Lower the results pressure
lower_results_pressure.description: Ask the board for a little more breathing room in the sporting demands of the active plan.
lower_results_pressure.tradeoffPreview: If they say yes, they typically expect tighter financial discipline.

more_youth_focus.label: More youth focus
more_youth_focus.description: Push the plan in a clearer youth direction with more room for development.
more_youth_focus.tradeoffPreview: If they say yes, the U25 identity becomes more central to the active plan.

more_results_focus.label: More results focus now
more_results_focus.description: Ask the board to weight top results higher right away.
more_results_focus.tradeoffPreview: This does not make the plan easier - the sporting demands get sharper.

ease_identity_requirements.label: Ease identity requirements
ease_identity_requirements.description: Ask for a little more flexibility in squad composition and identity goals.
ease_identity_requirements.tradeoffPreview: If they say yes, they typically turn up the sporting pressure instead.

requestReason.midCycleLocked: The {years}-year plan is too early in its cycle to be redirected. The board wants at least {percent}% of the plan completed or a major satisfaction swing before a re-orientation.
requestReason.majorPivotUsed: The board has already accepted a major pivot in this plan cycle. Another big change of direction requires a fresh plan.
requestReason.fallback: The board declines the request right now.

lowerResults.noSportingGoals: The plan has no sporting goals to ease.
lowerResults.tooUnhappy: The board is too dissatisfied to ease the results demands.
lowerResults.needProgress: The board wants to see more progress before easing the results demands.
lowerResults.starPressure: Big profiles keep sponsor expectations high, so the board will not ease the results demands yet.
lowerResults.underEnoughPressure: The board already feels the plan is under enough pressure and wants to see more progress before easing the demands.
lowerResults.starAmbitionLocked: The board refuses to lower the ambition level for a team with clear star profiles, because sponsor expectations are already raised.

moreYouth.alreadyYouth: The plan is already on a youth track.
moreYouth.noIdentityGoal: The plan lacks an identity goal to redirect.
moreYouth.needStability: The board wants to see more stability before switching focus now.
moreYouth.needYouthBase: The board wants to see a clearer youth base in the squad before switching focus.

moreResults.alreadyResults: The plan is already pushing for top results.
moreResults.squadTooThin: The board wants to see a broader squad before raising the ambition level further.

easeIdentity.noIdentityGoal: The plan has no identity requirement to ease.
easeIdentity.needTrust: The board wants more trust before easing the identity requirement.
easeIdentity.needSportingStability: The board wants to see more sporting stability before easing the identity requirement.
easeIdentity.nationalCoreCentral: The board sees the national core as a vital part of the team's DNA and will not let it go yet.
easeIdentity.youthCoreCentral: The board sees the youth track as a core of the team's identity and will not let it go yet.
easeIdentity.needStabilityFirst: The board will not ease the identity requirements until the team stands more stable on the sporting side.
easeIdentity.nationalCoreDna: The board sees the national core as a vital part of the team's DNA and will not let it go yet.

lowerResults.titlePartial: The board gives a little slack
lowerResults.titleTradeoff: The board gives slack at a price
lowerResults.summaryStar: The board only gives a little slack, because a team with big profiles is still held to high expectations.
lowerResults.summaryDefault: The board slightly lowers the sporting pressure in the active plan.
lowerResults.tradeoffStar: The profiles give the sponsor project weight, but they also mean the board tightens the financial demand instead of letting the ambitions go entirely.
lowerResults.tradeoffEconomy: In return the financial demand gets sharper, so the team must be run with more discipline for the rest of the plan.
lowerResults.tradeoffPartial: The board only grants a partial easing, because the plan still needs clear results.

moreYouth.titleBridge: The board only accepts a gradual shift
moreYouth.titleDefault: The board accepts a more youthful track
moreYouth.summaryBridge: The board wants to see more development, but a team with clear star profiles cannot switch tracks all at once.
moreYouth.summaryYouthTrack: The board already sees a youth track in the squad and turns the plan more clearly towards development.
moreYouth.summaryNationalCore: The board sees a clear core in the squad and accepts turning the plan towards a more long-term development direction.
moreYouth.summaryDefault: The plan is turned more towards development and long-term squad building.
moreYouth.tradeoffBridge: The plan becomes more youth-oriented, but the board keeps the focus at a balanced waypoint and does not let go of the results pressure entirely yet.
moreYouth.tradeoffDefault: In return the U25 identity is now a clearer and more lasting requirement in the active plan.

moreResults.titleBridge: The board only accepts a gradual escalation
moreResults.summaryBridge: The board wants to see more results pressure, but a pronounced youth track is only moved gradually towards a more ambitious middle position.
moreResults.summaryStar: Big profiles and sponsor expectations make the board raise the ambition right away.
moreResults.summarySpecialized: The board reads the team as ready to chase bigger results and raises the ambition.
moreResults.summaryDefault: The plan now weights top results even more clearly than before.
moreResults.tradeoffBridge: The board holds on to part of the development track, so the team must prove the new ambition level over time.
moreResults.tradeoffDefault: You get a little more flexibility in the identity requirement, but the results goals have in return become sharper right away.

easeIdentity.titleCore: The board only eases the identity requirement slightly
easeIdentity.titleDefault: The board eases the identity requirement
easeIdentity.summaryCore: The board still sees the national core as a vital part of the team's DNA and only gives a little more flexibility in the identity requirement.
easeIdentity.summaryDefault: The team gets a little more flexibility in squad building and the identity-bearing goals.
easeIdentity.tradeoffCore: The national identity is not let go entirely, and in return the board expects sharper sporting output for the rest of the plan.
easeIdentity.tradeoffDefault: In return the board expects sharper sporting output for the rest of the plan.
